title: Resource-fair quantum charging advantage
open: Demonstrate a scalable quantum-battery charging advantage after matching classical and quantum devices for charger energy, interaction strength, control complexity, preparation, and readout costs.
status: Collective-charging advantages are established in models, with preliminary experiments; a broadly convincing end-to-end advantage remains outstanding.
why: Determines whether quantum batteries offer useful energy technology rather than an advantageous comparison convention.
key_works: F. Campaioli et al. (2024), *Colloquium: Quantum batteries*, DOI:10.1103/RevModPhys.96.031001.

title: Predictive thermal conductance of real interfaces
open: Predict thermal boundary conductance from a manufacturable interface’s chemistry, roughness, contamination, bonding, and intermixing, with uncertainty bounds that transfer across fabrication processes.
status: Acoustic and diffuse-mismatch models capture limited regimes; atomistic calculations and interface-mode measurements have not produced a universal practical predictor.
why: Interface resistance limits electronics cooling, thermoelectrics, and high-power energy devices.
key_works: A. Giri and P. E. Hopkins (2020), *A Review of Experimental and Computational Advances in Thermal Boundary Conductance and Nanoscale Thermal Transport across Solid Interfaces*, DOI:10.1002/adfm.201903857.

title: Tight energy bounds for metal-mediated nitrogen fixation
open: Establish achievable minimum full-cycle energy costs for metal-mediated ammonia synthesis when metal regeneration, solvent recovery, proton delivery, separation, and side reactions are all included.
status: A 2025 analysis derives limits for specified electrodeposited-metal pathways; broader reaction networks and practical attainability remain unresolved.
why: Identifies which catalyst improvements can actually reduce system energy consumption.
key_works: V. Azumah and V. Viswanathan (2025), *Fundamental Limits of Dissociative Electrochemical Ammonia Synthesis via Electrodeposited Metals*, arXiv:2507.21121.

title: Reversible solid-state sulfur conversion
open: Maintain ionic and electronic contact through sulfur conversion and volume changes without excessive pressure, inactive conductive additives, or low areal capacity.
status: Solid-state lithium–sulfur architectures are demonstrated; practical feasibility depends on simultaneous mechanical and transport constraints.
why: Could reduce shuttle-related losses while preserving sulfur’s energy advantage.
key_works: G. Wang et al. (2025), *Assessing the practical feasibility of solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries*, DOI:10.1038/s43246-025-00918-9.

title: Reproducible aqueous nitrogen reduction
subfield: Fuel cells, ammonia, and electrochemical fuels
open: Demonstrate useful ammonia production from nitrogen in aqueous electrochemical systems with rigorous isotope controls, contamination exclusion, complete balances, and independent replication.
status: A 2019 protocol addressed widespread measurement pitfalls; analytical rigor does not itself establish a practical synthesis route.
why: Separates genuine nitrogen fixation from trace-contamination artifacts.
key_works: S. Z. Andersen et al. (2019), *A rigorous electrochemical ammonia synthesis protocol with quantitative isotope measurements*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-019-1260-x.

title: Grid-forming recovery after current saturation
open: Design converters that return predictably from current-limited fault operation to normal grid-forming behavior without loss of synchronization or damaging secondary transients.
status: Current limitation is necessary for semiconductor protection; its interaction with grid-forming dynamics remains a central control problem.
why: Fault survival requires more than avoiding immediate device destruction.
key_works: Lin et al. (2020), grid-forming inverter roadmap, NREL/TP-5D00-73476.

title: Convergence of all-orders near-axis expansions
open: Establish convergence radii or useful remainder bounds for stellarator near-axis expansions, including finite pressure, rather than only generating formal coefficients to arbitrary order.
status: An all-orders axis-expansion framework was developed in 2024. Formal solvability does not establish convergence at the finite minor radius needed by an actual device.
why: Converts a powerful design construction into a quantitatively certified approximation.
key_works: W. Sengupta et al. (2024), *Stellarator equilibrium axis-expansion to all orders in distance from the axis for arbitrary plasma beta*, arXiv:2402.17034; DOI:10.1017/S002237782400076X.

title: A physically calibrated quasisymmetry-error metric
open: Develop a computable quasisymmetry-error measure with bounds on relevant transport or particle-loss observables across energy, pitch angle, collisionality, and equilibrium variation.
status: Existing measures need not rank configurations consistently. The 2022 comparison of quasisymmetry measures demonstrates why minimizing a convenient geometric norm is not equivalent to minimizing every physical loss.
why: Prevents optimization from improving a surrogate while worsening confinement.
key_works: E. Rodríguez, E. J. Paul, and A. Bhattacharjee (2022), *Measures of quasisymmetry for stellarators*, arXiv:2109.13080; DOI:10.1017/S0022377821001331.

title: Collisional boundary layers in piecewise-omnigenous fields
open: Determine the transport produced near boundaries between differently trapped orbit classes in piecewise-omnigenous fields, including collisions, finite orbit width, and realistic smoothing of idealized geometry.
status: Piecewise omnigenity was introduced in 2024 with favorable transport properties. The construction does not eliminate the need to resolve transitions between orbit regions.
why: Tests whether a larger, more manufacturable confinement family retains its apparent transport advantage.
key_works: J. L. Velasco et al. (2024), *Piecewise omnigenous stellarators*, arXiv:2405.07634; DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.185101.

title: Predicting pedestal density without prescribing it
open: Predict pedestal density and temperature profiles jointly from fueling, recycling, neutral penetration, turbulence, and stability rather than supplying density as an external input to a pedestal-height model.
status: EPED established a successful stability-based framework for pedestal height and width. A closed prediction of particle balance and the entire pedestal state is a stronger requirement.
why: Density assumptions strongly affect predicted fusion performance and operating margins.
key_works: P. B. Snyder et al. (2011), *A first-principles predictive model of the pedestal height and width: development, testing and ITER optimization with the EPED model*.

title: Predictive isotope scaling of core heat transport
open: Explain and predict how replacing hydrogen, deuterium, or tritium changes heat transport while independently controlling heating deposition, density profiles, rotation, and impurity content.
status: A 2025 JET study combines deuterium–tritium comparisons with gyrokinetic simulations. Agreement for selected discharges does not establish a transferable isotope-scaling law.
why: Reduces uncertainty when extrapolating nontritium experiments to burning plasmas.
key_works: JET Contributors (2025), *Experimental study and gyrokinetic simulations of isotope effects on core heat transport in JET tokamak deuterium and tritium plasmas*, DOI:10.1088/1741-4326/adab04.

title: Reactor-relevant impurity seeding in negative triangularity
open: Maintain favorable confinement and particle exhaust while radiating a large fraction of input power using reactor-relevant impurities, without unacceptable core accumulation.
status: Highly radiating negative-triangularity plasmas have been demonstrated; the remaining problem is a transferable operating window with self-consistent impurity transport.
why: A confinement configuration must also solve its exhaust problem.
key_works: L. Casali et al. (2025), *Achievement of highly radiating plasmas in negative triangularity and effect of reactor-relevant seeded impurities on confinement and transport*; A. Marinoni, O. Sauter, and S. Coda (2021), *A brief history of negative triangularity tokamak plasmas*.

title: Reactor-scale scrape-off-layer heat-width prediction
open: Predict divertor heat-flux width across the transition from present devices to reactor-scale plasmas, resolving the competing roles of magnetic drifts, turbulence, and machine size.
status: Heuristic scaling and large kinetic simulations provide different forms of evidence. A validated extrapolation across the relevant regime change remains necessary.
why: Small errors in heat width translate into large errors in component heat loading.
key_works: R. J. Goldston (2012), *Heuristic drift-based model of the power scrape-off width in low-gas-puff H-mode tokamaks*; PPPL (2021), research account of XGC reactor-scale divertor-heat-load simulations.

title: Nonlocal parallel heat-flux closure without tuning
open: Replace empirical flux limiters with reduced closures that reproduce kinetic parallel heat transport through steep, evolving edge gradients without discharge-specific tuning.
status: Nonlocal kernels and kinetic comparisons were developed in 2018, and subsequent scrape-off-layer studies incorporated nonlocal transport. General accuracy across rapidly changing collisionality remains unresolved.
why: Improves predictions of detachment, transient heat loads, and target temperatures.
key_works: G. Ciraolo et al. (2018), *Fluid and kinetic modelling for non-local heat transport in magnetic fusion devices*, arXiv:1801.01177; DOI:10.1002/ctpp.201700222.

title: Error-controlled switching between runaway-electron models
open: Construct adaptive models that switch between reduced and kinetic runaway descriptions while preserving the evolving distribution and bounding errors in predicted seed populations.
status: Olasz et al. identified a collision-timescale criterion for failure of quasi-stationary Dreicer approximations in 2021. A complete error-controlled switching scheme is a stronger requirement.
why: Makes integrated disruption simulations affordable without silently losing essential kinetic memory.
key_works: S. Olasz et al. (2021), *Validity of models for Dreicer generation of runaway electrons in dynamic scenarios*, arXiv:2101.02740; DOI:10.1088/1741-4326/abf0de.

title: Tritium inventory from evolving tungsten defect populations
open: Infer and predict retained tritium when irradiation defects, helium bubbles, grain boundaries, and surface deposits evolve during service rather than remaining fixed trapping sites.
status: Laboratory retention studies identify strong material-history effects. Extrapolating those measurements to simultaneous neutron, thermal, and plasma exposure remains unresolved.
why: Connects material degradation to recoverable fuel inventory and component handling.
key_works: E. Bernard et al. (2019), *Tritium retention in W plasma-facing materials: Impact of…* — full subtitle **(verify)**, Nuclear Materials and Energy, article PII:S2352179118302424.

title: Spatiotemporal mix reconstruction from radiochemical products
open: Recover when, where, and how much ablator material mixed with fuel using radiochemical products together with other diagnostics, while quantifying nonuniqueness.
status: A 2025 study measured technetium–molybdenum isotope ratios across a NIF campaign. Integrated product yields constrain mix but do not uniquely reconstruct its complete history.
why: Distinguishes different failure mechanisms that produce similar final yields.
key_works: K. N. Kmak et al. (2025), *Using radiochemistry to diagnose fuel-ablator mix in inertial confinement fusion studies at the National Ignition Facility…*, DOI:10.3389/fchem.2025.1632948.

title: Where the solid-electrolyte interphase actually grows
open: Determine the reaction locations and moving growth fronts within heterogeneous interphases as electrolyte composition, electrode potential, and age change.
status: Isotope-assisted depth profiling demonstrated bottom-up growth in a studied system in 2018. A single mechanism should not be assumed universal across chemistries and cycling histories.
why: Growth location determines which species must cross the interphase and how passivation can be improved.
key_works: Z. Liu et al. (2018), *A Bottom-Up Formation Mechanism of Solid Electrolyte Interphase Revealed by Isotope-Assisted Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry*, DOI:10.1021/acs.jpclett.8b02350.

title: Separating calendar corrosion from cycling-induced lithium loss
open: Quantify lithium consumption during rest independently of deposition and stripping losses, including changes caused by state of charge and previous morphology.
status: In-situ NMR has resolved both dead-lithium formation and corrosion. A transferable model for arbitrary rest–cycle histories remains more demanding than identifying both mechanisms.
why: High cycling efficiency can coexist with poor calendar life.
key_works: Gunnarsdóttir et al. (2020), *Noninvasive In Situ NMR Study of “Dead Lithium” Formation and Lithium Corrosion in Full-Cell Lithium Metal Batteries*, PMCID:PMC7729915.

title: Enumerating stable states of lossy grids with realistic controls
open: Extend topology-based enumeration of synchronous states to networks with voltage dynamics, reactive-power limits, converter controls, and protection transitions.
status: Delabays, Jafarpour, and Bullo showed how winding partitions organize multiple states in lossy oscillator models. Their analysis also shows that dissipation can increase multistability.
why: Reveals stable but undesirable operating states missed by a single initialization.
key_works: R. Delabays, S. Jafarpour, and F. Bullo (2022), *Multistability and anomalies in oscillator models of lossy power grids*, arXiv:2202.02439; DOI:10.1038/s41467-022-32931-8.

title: Elimination or certification of spurious state-estimation minima
open: Characterize when nonlinear state estimators possess misleading local minima, and develop algorithms that either avoid them or certify that a returned estimate is globally adequate.
status: Spurious local minima have been studied explicitly. Convexity or benign behavior in a restricted formulation does not establish it for every measurement layout.
why: A numerically converged estimate can still be physically wrong.
key_works: R. Y. Zhang and J. Lavaei (2019), *Spurious Local Minima in Power System State Estimation*.

title: Braess-safe network reinforcement
open: Identify network additions or capacity upgrades that cannot worsen specified congestion or stability metrics over a defined uncertainty set, or derive conditions showing when such guarantees are impossible.
status: Braess-type worsening in power grids has been analyzed and demonstrated in models. The existence of the paradox is solved context; safe intervention selection remains open.
why: More infrastructure does not automatically improve every network outcome.
key_works: B. Schäfer et al. (2022), *Understanding Braess’ paradox in power grids*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-022-32917-6.

title: Atomic identity of LeTID-active defect complexes
open: Identify the defect complexes and charge-state transitions responsible for light- and elevated-temperature-induced degradation across relevant silicon materials and processing histories.
status: Hydrogen-based explanations reproduce important observations, but reproducing degradation kinetics is not equivalent to uniquely identifying the microscopic defect.
why: Enables targeted prevention instead of process recipes that work only empirically.
key_works: D. Chen et al. (2020), *Hydrogen-induced degradation: Explaining the mechanism behind light- and elevated temperature-induced degradation in n- and p-type silicon*, DOI:10.1016/j.solmat.2019.110353.

title: Energy-selective contacts without excessive heat leakage
open: Build hot-carrier contacts that extract a narrow energy range while retaining useful electrical conductance and suppressing unwanted heat exchange.
status: Nonideal-contact analysis quantifies how heat flow undermines hot-carrier conversion. Perfectly selective model contacts do not establish a realizable device.
why: Slow cooling in an absorber is insufficient without a compatible extraction mechanism.
key_works: A. S. Sharma et al. (2023), *Heat Flow through Nonideal Contacts in Hot-Carrier Solar Cells*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevApplied.20.034001.

title: Perovskite reverse-bias survival under realistic shading
open: Prevent irreversible local damage when module-level shading forces perovskite cells into reverse bias, including repeated events and realistic protection circuitry.
status: Improved reverse-bias stability has been demonstrated through contact and electrode design. That does not establish lifetime survival across module fault and shading histories.
why: Ordinary outdoor shading must not become a destructive electrochemical event.
key_works: F. Jiang et al. (2024), *Improved reverse bias stability in p–i–n perovskite solar cells with optimized hole transport materials and less reactive electrodes*, Nature Energy 9, 1275–1284.

title: Persistent permeability beyond conventional brittle behavior
open: Create connected flow paths in superhot rock and demonstrate that they remain useful under the temperatures, stresses, and chemical conditions expected during prolonged circulation.
status: Watanabe et al. demonstrated cloud-fracture networks in high-temperature experiments. Initial permeability creation does not establish long-duration reservoir performance.
why: Determines whether accessible superhot rock can become a usable heat exchanger.
key_works: N. Watanabe et al. (2019), *Cloud-fracture networks as a means of accessing superhot geothermal energy*, PMCID:PMC6353971.

title: Freeze-plug actuation across the full reactor operating history
open: Demonstrate reliable passive thawing and drainage following loss of active cooling across low-power, startup, shutdown, and nominal-power thermal histories.
status: A 2019 molten-salt fast-reactor study shows that thawing behavior depends strongly on geometry and available heating. Passive actuation cannot be assumed from material melting temperature alone.
why: The shutdown mechanism must function when the preceding operating state is unfavorable.
key_works: M. Tiberga et al. (2019), *Preliminary investigation on the melting behavior of a freeze-valve for the Molten Salt Fast Reactor*.

title: Maintaining the protective oxygen window in lead coolants
open: Control oxygen activity throughout a lead or lead–bismuth circuit so protective surface layers persist without excessive oxide precipitation, including cold regions, transients, and changing material inventories.
status: Oxygen management is an established corrosion-control strategy. The 2022 materials assessment documents competing dissolution, oxidation, and precipitation processes that prevent one nominal bulk oxygen concentration from guaranteeing protection everywhere.
why: A chemistry setting that protects one component can foul or damage another.
key_works: X. Gong et al. (2022), *Environmental degradation of structural materials in liquid lead- and lead-bismuth eutectic-cooled reactors*, DOI:10.1016/j.pmatsci.2022.100920.

title: Long-horizon effects of intermittent water ingress in pitch bearings
open: Predict damage from repeated episodes of water contamination, drying, lubricant replacement, and changing loads, rather than treating water content as a fixed test parameter.
status: Short-term pitch-bearing water-ingress experiments were reported in 2024. They do not determine whether apparently recoverable contamination leaves latent damage that accelerates later wear.
why: Maintenance decisions depend on whether removing contaminated grease restores the bearing or merely hides continuing damage.
key_works: M. Stammler et al. (2024), pitch-bearing water-ingress study, Lubricants 12, 310, DOI:10.3390/lubricants12090310.

title: Field-calibrated fatigue prediction for large roller pitch bearings
open: Validate rolling-contact fatigue calculations against sufficiently representative service histories, including ring deformation, manufacturing variation, lubrication, and nonuniform roller loading.
status: Menck, Schleich, and Stammler developed detailed fatigue calculations for a three-row roller pitch bearing in 2025. Numerical stress resolution does not itself validate accumulated lifetime damage.
why: Accurate contact mechanics must translate into credible failure probabilities and replacement intervals.
key_works: O. Menck, F. Schleich, and M. Stammler (2025), *Rolling contact fatigue calculation of a three-row roller pitch bearing in a wind turbine*, DOI:10.5194/wes-10-2771-2025.

title: Long-lived oxygen-tolerant electrochemical carbon capture
open: Maintain capture capacity and electrochemical efficiency in oxygen-containing feeds over long campaigns, including water variability and accumulation of trace reaction products.
status: Abdinejad and colleagues demonstrated an oxygen-stable redox-active capture chemistry in 2024. Oxygen tolerance in a selected experiment is not equivalent to complete long-term electrolyte stability.
why: Avoiding oxygen removal is valuable only if the capture medium survives direct exposure.
key_works: M. Abdinejad et al. (2024), *Oxygen-Stable Electrochemical CO2 Capture using Redox-Active Heterocyclic Benzodithiophene Quinone*, DOI:10.1002/anie.202412229.

title: Transferable annual algal-productivity forecasts
open: Predict annual recoverable biomass across sites using weather, strain selection, crop rotation, harvesting, contamination, and downtime rather than extrapolating peak seasonal growth.
status: McGowen and colleagues demonstrated annual productivity improvements through crop rotation and operational management in 2023.
why: Fuel and bioproduct economics depend on annual output from the complete cultivation system.
key_works: J. McGowen et al. (2023), *Outdoor annual algae productivity improvements at the pre-pilot scale through crop rotation and pond operational management strategies*, DOI:10.1016/j.algal.2023.102995.

title: High boron rejection without excessive desalination penalties
open: Reject neutral boron species at relevant feed conditions while preserving water permeability, membrane stability, and acceptable pressure or chemical-adjustment requirements.
status: Huang and colleagues improved boron rejection and permeability using tailored thin-film nanocomposite membranes in 2025. Promising coupons do not establish durable module performance in real seawater.
why: Meeting boron specifications can otherwise require additional treatment that increases energy and complexity.
key_works: J. Huang et al. (2025), *Enhanced boron rejection and permeability of thin-film nanocomposite membranes via g-C₃N₄-tuned diffusion and reaction*, DOI:10.1016/j.desal.2025.118902.

title: Whole-cycle validation of ultrasonic water extraction
open: Demonstrate that reduced extraction energy translates into lower complete-device energy per unit of usable water after capture, airflow, electronics, and recovery are included.
status: Shuvo and colleagues reported a large extraction-stage energy improvement in 2025. That comparison should not be interpreted as the same improvement in every component or in total water-production energy.
why: Component-level advantages can be diluted or reversed by the rest of the device.
key_works: I. I. Shuvo et al. (2025), *High-efficiency atmospheric water harvesting enabled by ultrasonic extraction*, DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-65586-2.

title: Scalable synthesis of genuinely ordered bulk tetrataenite
open: Produce substantial quantities of ordered L1₀ FeNi at practical processing times and temperatures, with independently verified ordering rather than diffraction features attributable to other phases.
status: A prominent 2022 bulk-casting claim was reinterpreted and retracted; 2025 work re-examines phosphorus-assisted ordering. The corrected evidence does not establish that phosphorus alone solves rapid bulk production.
why: Tetrataenite remains attractive only if its ordered phase can be manufactured reliably rather than obtained through geological timescales or ambiguous measurements.
key_works: S. R. Maness, S. M. Pennell, and D. C. Dunand (2025), *Investigating the effect of phosphorus on L1₀ ordering in melt-solidified Fe-Ni alloys*, DOI:10.1016/j.mtla.2025.102617.

title: Tetrataenite microstructures with useful permanent-magnet coercivity
open: Combine chemical ordering with grain size, texture, defects, and domain structure that produce useful coercivity and energy product at bulk scale.
status: Houghton and colleagues emphasize that identifying an ordered phase is not equivalent to producing an effective permanent magnet. Suitable magnetic microstructure remains an additional requirement.
why: A material can possess favorable intrinsic anisotropy while remaining a poor practical magnet.
key_works: O. S. Houghton et al. (2025), *Reinterpretation of Report of Tetrataenite in Bulk Alloy Castings*, DOI:10.1002/advs.202408796.

title: Electrolyte removal without damaging recyclable graphite
open: Remove electrolyte residues and decomposition products while preserving graphite properties and minimizing solvent use, thermal treatment, and secondary emissions.
status: Rothermel and colleagues compared graphite-recycling approaches, including carbon-dioxide-assisted extraction, in 2016. A method effective for one returned-cell stream may not tolerate different binders and electrolyte histories.
why: Purification can destroy part of the material value that recycling is intended to preserve.
key_works: S. Rothermel et al. (2016), *Graphite Recycling from Spent Lithium-Ion Batteries*, DOI:10.1002/cssc.201601062.

title: Predicting strontium-vanadate cathode burn-in
open: Predict the time-dependent emitting state of SrVO₃ from temperature, oxygen activity, surface termination, and prior operation, then identify preparation conditions that reliably produce stable emission.
status: Experiments published in 2024 document substantial changes in emission during extended heating, associated with evolving surface composition. Initial work-function measurements therefore do not establish operating performance.
why: A reproducible low-work-function material is useful only if its favorable surface survives and can be manufactured consistently.
key_works: M. S. Sheikh et al. (2024), *Time dependence of SrVO3 thermionic electron emission properties*, DOI:10.1063/5.0186012.

title: Transferring near-unity quantum yield into the visible spectrum
open: Achieve comparably efficient overall water splitting under visible photons while retaining stoichiometric gas production, catalyst stability, and useful solar-to-hydrogen efficiency.
status: Takata and colleagues reported approximately 96% apparent quantum yield at 350–365 nm in 2020. That ultraviolet result is not 96% solar-to-hydrogen efficiency and does not establish equivalent visible-light performance.
why: Solar usefulness depends on the captured spectrum as well as the efficiency of individual absorbed photons.
key_works: T. Takata et al. (2020), *Photocatalytic water splitting with a quantum efficiency of almost unity*, DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2278-9.

title: Simultaneous high efficiency and decade-scale PEC lifetime
open: Demonstrate the paired requirements represented by DOE’s historical ultimate target: 25% solar-to-hydrogen efficiency and ten years of operation before output falls to 80% of its initial value.
status: These are historical program targets, not a newly issued standard or an achieved combined result. High-efficiency demonstrations, including a 19% monolithic device, do not establish decade-scale qualification.
why: Efficiency and lifetime jointly determine whether semiconductor-intensive direct solar hydrogen is economical.
key_works: DOE, *Technical Targets for Hydrogen Production: Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting*; W. H. Cheng et al. (2018), *Monolithic photoelectrochemical device for direct water splitting with 19% efficiency*.

title: Low-loss ion separation in a closed ionocaloric refrigerator
open: Reduce the work of restoring the working mixture after ion-induced melting while preserving useful cooling rate, temperature lift, and cycle efficiency.
status: Lilley and Prasher demonstrated an ionocaloric refrigeration cycle in 2022. The existence of the cycle is established; competitive, durable separation and regeneration at useful scale remain the engineering target.
why: A large phase-change cooling effect does not eliminate the work needed to reset the mixture.
key_works: D. Lilley and R. Prasher (2022), *Ionocaloric refrigeration cycle*, DOI:10.1126/science.ade1696.

title: Is a packed plasma catalyst actually catalyzing the surface reaction?
open: Separate chemical surface catalysis from changes in discharge geometry, local fields, heating, and plasma composition caused by inserting packing material.
status: Ndayirinde and colleagues found that packed catalysts acted principally as plasma modifiers in their 2023 ammonia experiments. A yield change upon adding a catalyst therefore does not, by itself, establish surface catalysis.
why: Otherwise, catalyst screening can optimize an electrical packing effect while assigning it the wrong chemical explanation.
key_works: C. Ndayirinde et al. (2023), *Plasma-catalytic ammonia synthesis: Packed catalysts act as plasma modifiers*, DOI:10.1016/j.cattod.2023.114156.

title: Product removal that preserves plasma-synthesis efficiency
open: Integrate ammonia capture and regeneration with plasma synthesis so suppressing back-reaction yields a net benefit after separation, recycle, and pressure losses.
status: Lower product concentration can reduce undesired reverse reactions, but it also creates a harder downstream separation problem.
why: An improved reactor can become a worse complete process.
key_works: Lefferts (2024), plasma-catalysis perspective, DOI:10.1002/ange.202305322.

title: Hydrodynamic limit of the piston model
open: Derive the macroscopic heat equation from the piston energy-exchange process, with a justified transport coefficient and controlled initial conditions.
status: The 2026 workshop account distinguishes obtaining a Markov process in a rare-interaction limit from obtaining its hydrodynamic limit; it explicitly lists the latter as unresolved.
why: A stochastic description of microscopic exchanges is not yet a derivation of Fourier-scale transport.
key_works: Szász (2026), *Fourier law from Hamiltonian dynamics*, discussing the Bálint–Nándori–Szász–Tóth piston-model program.

title: Distinguishing wind changes from airborne sensor failure
open: Determine when kite measurements uniquely identify wind, aerodynamic changes, and sensor faults, and specify the minimum additional sensing needed when they do not.
status: Cayon, Watson, and Schmehl documented cases where sensor saturation or modeling errors produced misleading inferred winds. Constraining an estimated wind component can suppress artifacts while also hiding real flow.
why: A controller should not respond to an instrument artifact as though it were a gust.
key_works: O. Cayon, S. Watson, and R. Schmehl (2025), *Kite as a sensor: wind and state estimation in tethered flying systems*, DOI:10.5194/wes-10-2161-2025.

title: Closed-loop prediction of suspended control-unit swing
open: Predict coupled wing and suspended-control-unit motion when aerodynamic forces and steering evolve dynamically, rather than prescribing the measured wing trajectory.
status: Schelbergen and Schmehl’s 2024 analysis reproduces important swinging behavior using a two-mass representation, but deliberately excludes parts of unconstrained aerodynamic and yaw dynamics.
why: Swinging changes bridle loads, attitude measurements, and the effectiveness of control actions.
key_works: M. Schelbergen and R. Schmehl (2024), *Swinging motion of a kite with suspended control unit flying turning manoeuvres*, DOI:10.5194/wes-9-1323-2024.

title: Cycle-to-cycle evolution of recyclable iron-powder morphology
open: Predict whether repeated oxidation and reduction drive particle size, internal porosity, cracks, and phase distribution toward a stable population or progressive fragmentation.
status: Choisez and colleagues resolved major microstructural transformations during iron-powder combustion in 2022. Characterizing one transformation does not determine the trajectory of many complete recycling cycles.
why: Reaction rates and collection requirements may change as the fuel is reused.
key_works: L. Choisez et al. (2022), *Phase transformations and microstructure evolution during combustion of iron powder*, DOI:10.1016/j.actamat.2022.118261.

title: Mechanism-resolved activation of TiFe hydrogen-storage alloys
open: Determine when activation is controlled by surface oxide conversion, catalytic surface species, secondary phases, or exposure of fresh material through cracking.
status: TiFe has decades of successful activation methods, but different preparation and exposure histories support different explanations. The open problem is predictive mechanism selection, not first activation of TiFe.
why: Reliable low-temperature commissioning requires more than reproducing one preparation recipe.
key_works: T. Schober (1983), *On the activation of FeTi for hydrogen storage*, DOI:10.1016/0022-5088(83)90249-7; E. M. Dematteis et al. (2021), *Substitutional effects in TiFe for hydrogen storage*, DOI:10.1039/D1MA00101A.

title: Testing temperature-dependent coherent phase transformation in palladium hydride
open: Experimentally distinguish coherent two-phase transformation from nearly homogeneous hydrogen uptake as temperature, specimen size, and defect-mediated strain relaxation change.
status: Rahm, Löfgren, and Erhart’s calculations predict a change in transformation character around 400 K under their coherent-system assumptions. Real specimens introduce relaxation pathways that must be separated from the predicted effect.
why: Hysteresis determines recoverable work and operating pressures in reversible hydrogen storage.
key_works: J. M. Rahm, J. Löfgren, and P. Erhart (2022), *Quantitative predictions of thermodynamic hysteresis: Temperature-dependent character of the phase transition in Pd–H*, DOI:10.1016/j.actamat.2022.117697; arXiv:2110.07883.

title: Desiccants that do not destroy fluoronitrile insulating gas
open: Remove water from C₄F₇N/CO₂ insulation systems without catalyzing gas decomposition or introducing products from degradation of the desiccant itself.
status: Gao and colleagues’ nine-month aging study found incompatibility for the tested zeolite sieve and possible decomposition of the tested organic alternative. High adsorption area can intensify unwanted chemistry.
why: A component intended to protect insulation can instead degrade the insulating medium.
key_works: W. Gao et al. (2021), *Compatibility of Molecular Sieves with C₄F₇N/CO₂ Insulating Gas Mixture*, DOI:10.1109/CEIDP50766.2021.9705379.

title: Spatial validation of HVDC cable aging during polarity reversal
open: Validate where insulation damage accumulates during voltage-polarity reversals, including the influence of temperature-dependent conductivity and residual charge.
status: Diban and colleagues’ 2024 model predicts strongly nonuniform lifetime reduction, especially in inner insulation. This is modeled damage distribution, not direct lifetime validation.
why: Average electric-field stress can conceal the region that governs failure.
key_works: B. Diban et al. (2024), *Life Estimation of HVDC Cables Subjected to Fast and Slow Polarity Reversals*, DOI:10.3390/en17133182.

title: Identifiability limits for superconducting inter-tape contact networks
open: Determine which internal contact resistances can be uniquely reconstructed from accessible cable terminals, and which require additional excitations or sensors.
status: The TITO method improves contact-resistance inference by accounting for parallel current paths. It does not establish arbitrary spatial reconstruction of every internal contact.
why: Prevents overinterpreting a terminal measurement as a unique internal defect map.
key_works: R. Teyber et al. (2025), *Tape-in-tape-out: a new approach for in-situ contact resistance measurements in high temperature superconducting CORC cables*, DOI:10.1088/1361-6668/aded3b.

title: Whole-system energy advantage of conduction-cooled flux pumps
open: Determine when contactless flux pumping reduces total electricity consumption after alternating-field losses, cryocooler work, switching, and avoided current-lead heat loads are included.
status: Iftikhar and colleagues demonstrated conduction-cooled flux pumping below 77 K. Successful current injection does not by itself identify the most efficient operating temperature and excitation schedule.
why: Eliminating a warm-to-cold conductor can introduce other refrigeration burdens.
key_works: M. H. Iftikhar et al. (2025), *A compact conduction cooled flux pump operating below 77 K*, DOI:10.1088/1361-6668/adaf5c.

title: Radical-pathway selectivity during electrocatalytic heat release
open: Resolve the competition between desired quadricyclane-to-norbornadiene conversion and irreversible reactions after electron transfer, including electronic states inadequately described by a single reference configuration.
status: Franz and colleagues show strong substituent dependence and explicitly identify more advanced electronic-structure treatment as a remaining need.
why: Low triggering voltage is insufficient if it opens destructive reaction pathways.
key_works: E. Franz et al. (2025), *Tuning Electrocatalytic Energy Release in Norbornadiene Based Molecular Solar Thermal Systems Through Substituent Effects*, DOI:10.1002/chem.202502294.

title: Unambiguous rarefaction-shock identification in dense organic vapor
open: Observe a finite-amplitude rarefaction shock while independently excluding temperature inhomogeneity, fluid decomposition, and measurement artifacts, and verify the thermodynamic states required for its nonclassical interpretation.
status: The 2025 ASTER experiments report repeatable departures from classical gas dynamics near the working fluid’s thermal-stability limit. Such departures do not, by themselves, uniquely identify a rarefaction shock.
why: Tests a distinctive prediction of nonconvex-fluid thermodynamics relevant to dense-vapor machinery.
key_works: C. Medipati et al. (2025), *Rarefaction Shockwave Experiments in Dense Organic Vapours*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-92695-2_16; N. Chandrasekaran et al. (2024), *Nonclassical wave propagation measurements in the high temperature vapor of D6…*, DOI:10.1007/s00348-024-03843-8.

title: Magnetic damping of bidirectional metal-pad waves
open: Measure magnetic damping for interfacial modes varying in both horizontal directions, resolving the complex induced-current patterns rather than extrapolating from one-dimensional modes.
status: Hegde and colleagues validate magnetic damping only for the particular mode \(m=1,n=0\); bidirectional-mode validation is explicitly outstanding.
why: These modes participate in instabilities of conducting liquid layers.
key_works: Hegde, Herreman, and Horstmann (2025), *Stability theory for metal pad roll with consideration of viscous and magnetic damping*, arXiv:2507.18301.

title: Cold-electron control of mirror-expander heat losses
open: Predict the self-consistent potential and heat transport when secondary emission and local ionization supply cold electrons to the expander.
status: These electron sources are omitted from Tyushev and colleagues’ studied model and identified as relevant extensions. A collisionless injected distribution does not represent every operating boundary.
why: Boundary-created populations can change upstream confinement and exhaust power.
key_works: Tyushev et al. (2025), *Drift-kinetic PIC simulations of plasma flow and energy transport in the magnetic mirror configuration*, arXiv:2501.15604.

title: Charge-selective trapping with nonthermal ion mixtures
open: Predict and sustain selective centrifugal confinement when beam-like distributions replace Maxwellian mixtures, including the power required to maintain those distributions.
status: The ion-mixture study identifies qualitatively different selection possibilities for nonthermal populations but does not provide a complete kinetic operating model.
why: Nonthermal control may change which species are retained or removed.
key_works: Kolmes, Ochs, and Fisch (2025), *Ion Mix Can Invert Centrifugal Traps*, arXiv:2504.18634.

title: Suppressing alpha-induced neutron side reactions without sacrificing heating
open: Reduce energetic-alpha overlap with boron while maintaining sufficient useful alpha-energy transfer to the plasma.
status: The 2025 ash study distinguishes thermal-ash control from neutron-producing reactions involving fast alphas. Removing already thermalized helium does not solve that separate problem.
why: “Aneutronic” primary fuel does not eliminate all neutron-producing pathways.
key_works: Ochs, Kolmes, and Fisch (2025), *Preventing ash from poisoning proton-boron 11 fusion plasmas*, DOI:10.1063/5.0266369.

title: Identity of the intermediate state in lead zirconate
open: Determine when the narrow intermediate regime in PbZrO₃ is a distinct equilibrium phase, a mixture, or a kinetically retained structure.
status: Zhang and colleagues’ 2024 simulations reproduce major thermal behavior but not every reported intermediate state; its interpretation remains dependent on conditions and modeling.
why: Phase identity controls how switching pathways should be modeled.
key_works: H. Zhang et al. (2024), *Finite-temperature properties of antiferroelectric perovskite PbZrO3 from deep learning interatomic potential*, arXiv:2406.09011.

title: Microstructure-to-knee prediction through percolation
open: Predict when gradual pore blockage, contact loss, or conductive-network damage causes a sharp performance transition, using measurable microstructure rather than fitted knee locations.
status: Percolation and threshold mechanisms are recognized explanations for knees. Quantitative prediction across realistic evolving electrode networks remains incomplete.
why: Connects abrupt macroscopic aging to controllable microscopic design features.
key_works: Attia et al. (2022), *“Knees” in lithium-ion battery aging trajectories*, arXiv:2201.02891.

title: Thousand-cycle durability of immobilized protein separators
open: Achieve a **proposed 1,000 capture–release cycles with at least 90% retained useful separation performance**, including realistic contaminants and regeneration conditions.
status: Ye and colleagues demonstrated protein-functionalized magnetic particles with more than 90% retained activity over five studied cycles. That is proof of reuse, not evidence for the proposed longer-life target.
why: Protein replacement and regeneration can govern the economics of biologically inspired separation.
key_works: Q. Ye et al. (2025), *Group Separation of Rare Earth Elements by Protein-Functionalized Magnetic Nanoparticles*, DOI:10.1021/acsestengg.5c00508.

title: Ten-thousand-cycle qualification of COF air-capture sorbents
open: Meet a **proposed target of 10,000 representative capture–regeneration cycles with less than 10% loss of usable capacity**, including real-air contaminants and mechanically shaped material.
status: COF-999 research includes approximately one hundred-cycle laboratory durability evidence. That is encouraging but does not establish the proposed longer-life target.
why: Sorbent replacement can determine both capture cost and lifecycle environmental burden.
key_works: Zhou et al. (2024), COF-999 capture study, DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08080-x.

title: Exact nested-surface, non-axisymmetric vacuum fields
open: Construct an analytic, non-axisymmetric vacuum magnetic field in a torus embedded in ordinary three-dimensional space, with globally nested invariant surfaces and nontrivial rotational transform, or establish the relevant obstruction.
status: Special topological-torus constructions and approximate numerical configurations exist. The 2026 analytic pressure-supported equilibria do not automatically supply the corresponding vacuum-field construction.
why: Would clarify which confinement geometries can exist without plasma-current assistance.
key_works: W. Weitzner and W. Sengupta (2020), *Exact non-symmetric closed line vacuum magnetic fields in a topological torus*, Physics of Plasmas 27, 022509; Landreman (2026), arXiv:2609.26742.

title: Thermally isolated micrometre gaps that remain dimensionally stable
open: Meet a **proposed joint qualification target** of a 1–4 μm gap over a square-centimetre active area at temperatures above 1,500 K, with spacer conductance below approximately 10 mW cm⁻² K⁻¹ and no progressive gap collapse.
status: Micrometre-gap converters exist; the roadmap identifies support conduction and dimensional stability as coupled constraints.
why: Reducing space charge must not introduce overwhelming conductive heat leakage.
key_works: Bellucci et al. (2026), thermionic roadmap, DOI:10.1088/1361-6463/ae611e.

title: Experimental multijunction thermoradiative advantage
open: Demonstrate that a multijunction thermoradiative device outperforms a comparable single-junction device after interconnection, optical coupling, and thermal losses are counted.
status: A 2025 idealized analysis predicts relative efficiency and power improvements at a 500 K emitter and 300 K sink. These are calculated gains, not a completed multijunction experiment.
why: Establishes whether junction complexity produces a net benefit.
key_works: P. Bohm, A. K. Menon, and Z. M. Zhang (2025), *Fundamental advantages of multijunction thermoradiative cells*, DOI:10.1063/5.0273591.

title: Experimental separation of spin Thomson heating
open: Detect reversible heating or cooling proportional to both spin current and temperature gradient, and distinguish electron-mediated and magnon-mediated contributions where both are possible.
status: Spin-dependent Thomson responses have theoretical descriptions; the May 2026 experimental perspective identifies their observation as unresolved.
why: Determines whether distributed spin-dependent heating can supplement interface-localized thermal control.
key_works: Uchida and Hirai (2026), *Spin caloritronics: History and future prospects of experiments*, arXiv:2605.01692; A. Slachter et al. (2011), *Modeling of thermal spin transport and spin-orbit effects in ferromagnetic/nonmagnetic mesoscopic devices*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.84.174408.

title: Thousand-cycle retention for electrocatalytically discharged photoswitches
open: Meet a **proposed target** of at least 90% retained usable storage capacity after 1,000 complete charging–discharging cycles, including catalyst and electrolyte aging.
status: High single-discharge selectivity is reported for selected substituents. It does not determine cumulative full-cycle retention.
why: Small irreversible losses compound through repeated reuse.
key_works: Franz et al. (2025), electrocatalytic molecular-storage study, DOI:10.1002/chem.202502294.
